design.contrast: interruption versus equal-count, position- and folio-matched ordinary gap; include section and line-position nuisance controls
design.falsifier: No held-folio interaction after controls, or an effect explained by page position/line length alone, falsifies the reset-state mechanism; do not rescue it by changing boundary thresholds.
design.mechanism: A drawing interruption clears the active owner/item state and begins a new process segment; ordinary transcription spaces do not.
design.prediction: After interruptions, first fields have higher rates of explicit owner/item introduction and lower anaphoric continuation than after matched ordinary gaps, replicating across held folios and alternate readings.
design.related: DIC001_drawing_interruption_target; drawing_reset_segment_atlas; DIC001 limitations explicitly prohibit picture-ownership or translation claims
design.scope: cached admitted transcription and DIC001/segment-atlas boundary inventory only; feasibility unknown for a clean owner/item coding panel
design.unit: eligible interruption and matched ordinary gap on the same folio/page, with adjacent cached fields

summary: Test whether the 440 unanimous drawing interruptions define a semantic state reset: the first complete field after an interruption should reintroduce an owner or item cue, while an ordinary same-page gap should usually continue the prior state. This retains DIC001's distributed-reset result and the drawing-reset segment atlas, but does not infer picture ownership, words, or translation.
title: Drawing interruptions reset inherited process state

design.contrast: ordinary line break without interruption versus matched within-line continuation and interruption-adjacent line break
design.falsifier: A line-break penalty equal to or larger than the interruption penalty, replicated in held folios, falsifies nonreset continuity; do not reinterpret line ends as clauses after the fact.
design.mechanism: Physical line layout is not a semantic closure boundary; state continuity is broken by drawing interruption, not by line ending.
design.prediction: Owner/item recurrence and compatible argument slots remain continuous across ordinary line breaks at rates comparable to within-line continuations, but drop after interruptions; section-specific classes remain separate.
design.related: DIC001_drawing_interruption_target; drawing_reset_segment_atlas; SIDEQUEST_scribe_memory (historical proposal only); GDT791 line-boundary correction
design.scope: cached 30-page owner-spine and admitted prose selectors; feasibility unknown for complete state labels outside the released owner panel
design.unit: adjacent line pairs within cached running prose, stratified by interruption status and folio

summary: Test the rival to a line-as-clause reading: when no DIC001 drawing interruption occurs, a line break should preserve the active owner/item state into the next line, while an interruption should reset it. The proposal uses the same admitted segment and visual-owner scope but asks a different state-transition question from DIC001.
title: Ordinary line breaks preserve local owner and item state

design.contrast: edge occurrence versus matched non-edge occurrence, crossed with ordered register pair and section; leave-one-register-pair-out validation
design.falsifier: No held edge interaction, or improvement disappears when whole identity and host class are controlled, falsifies the handoff mechanism; a global class lead is not sufficient.
design.mechanism: A whole at a register boundary signals transfer of the active record or target between adjacent presentation modes; its role depends on the ordered source/target register pair.
design.prediction: A small set of whole forms shows reproducible edge-specific continuation/owner-slot changes for one or more ordered register pairs, beyond whole identity, position, section, and host-class baselines.
design.related: post_IL023_system_class_heterogeneity_correction; GDT790_panel_owner_image_grammar_overlay; GDT792_host_transfer; these predecessors do not test ordered register-edge interaction
design.scope: admitted visual-owner spine and cached text/register tags; feasibility unknown for enough held transition edges, and no new page access is assumed
design.unit: complete-whole occurrence within one field of a cached register transition, with non-edge occurrences of the same whole as controls

summary: Test whether complete whole forms at immediate transitions between running prose, local labels, and radial units act as handoff markers, rather than having one global meaning or merely reflecting section frequency. The design follows the post-IL023 correction by fitting register-specific classes and evaluates only an edge interaction.
title: Register-transition edges carry handoff roles

design.contrast: role association on all-reading intersection versus each reading-specific surface; hold out physical folios
design.falsifier: A role survives only in one reading, or vanishes when uncertain spaces are preserved, falsifies the semantic claim; do not promote a reading-specific form meaning.
design.mechanism: A genuine whole-level role is attached to the underlying inscription locus and is stable across admitted alternate readings.
design.prediction: A candidate role retains direction and material effect on the all-reading intersection and in at least two independent reading projections after section, position, and folio controls.
design.related: GDT859 alternate-reader alignment; GDT764 bounded fields; current route's explicit prohibition on treating EVA labels as phonetic units
design.scope: cached source-group atlas and admitted semantic occurrence panels; feasibility unknown for candidate roles lacking complete three-reading joins
design.unit: complete-whole occurrence with a raw-group identity and three available reading projections

summary: Treat ZL3b, IT2a, and RF1b as alternate readings of one manuscript and test a necessary condition for any proposed complete-whole role: the role contrast must remain when forms are joined at raw-group identity and evaluated under each reading. A role lead that exists only after one reading's spacing or glyph choice is not semantic evidence.
title: Semantic role must survive alternate raw readings

design.contrast: candidate whole's incompatible-slot rate versus matched control wholes with the same frequency, section, and position profile
design.falsifier: Repeated held-folio counterexamples in the preregistered incompatible slot, or no separation from frequency/position controls, rejects the role claim and leaves the whole opaque.
design.mechanism: A concrete role imposes a semantic incompatibility boundary, so an item-like whole cannot freely occupy a process-only slot (and conversely).
design.prediction: At least one independently held candidate role shows a low incompatible-slot rate with a fixed upper bound, while matched opaque controls do not; a positive association without exclusion is insufficient.
design.related: GDT770 target-masked valency tournament; GDT805 context-role discriminator; GDT762 role candidates; this proposal adds a negative necessary-condition gate rather than another role fit
design.scope: cached exact-whole occurrence panels and existing structural tags; feasibility unknown until compatible/incompatible slots are frozen without using the target outcomes
design.unit: complete-whole occurrence paired with a predeclared compatible/incompatible structural slot

summary: For any candidate role that claims a concrete function such as quantity carrier, nominal item, or process operator, test its required negative context: the same complete whole should be rare or absent in a preregistered incompatible slot after matching section, position, and neighboring frame. This is a counterexample screen, not a positive classifier.
title: A proposed role requires exclusion from incompatible slots

design.contrast: A-to-B frame transfer and B-to-A frame transfer versus matched non-synonym pairs with equal frequency and edit distance
design.falsifier: A directional transfer fails on held folios or is no better than matched non-synonym pairs, falsifying shared-role interchangeability; do not rescue with component decomposition.
design.mechanism: Shared semantic role licenses the same neighboring argument and closure frames in both directions, subject to register-specific controls.
design.prediction: A genuine same-role pair passes both directional held-folio transfers with stable slot polarity; one-direction-only pairs are classified as analogies or distinct roles.
design.related: GDT807 target-masked paragraph exchange; GDT746 whole analogy distribution; GDT770 valency masking; this freezes reciprocal direction as the necessary condition
design.scope: cached complete-field and whole-neighbor panels; feasibility unknown for pairs with fewer than two independent physical folios per direction
design.unit: ordered complete-whole frame: immediate left/right whole and structural tags around one target

summary: When two complete wholes are proposed as the same role or interchangeable variants, require reciprocal frame compatibility: each must occur in the other's independently observed left/right structural frames, with held examples in both directions. One-way analogical similarity cannot establish a shared meaning.
title: Candidate same-role wholes require reciprocal frame compatibility

design.binding: independent source or visual owner links for both A positions, with ambiguous crossings quarantined
design.contrast: A-B-A versus matched A-B-C and A-C-A windows with the same lengths and section
design.countermodel: A-B-A is a layout or template recurrence with no referential continuity; A positions should then match controls after section/position adjustment.
design.mechanism: B is a bounded intervening operation or qualification; repeated A reactivates the prior referent and inherits its slot.
design.prediction: The two A positions preserve owner/target and compatible slot tags more often than both controls, across held folios.
design.related: SIDEQUEST_semantic_aba_return_frame; GDT573 anaphoric phrase route; retained as a distinct window-level referent test
design.scope: cached complete fields and admitted owner-spine records; feasibility unknown until independent referent bindings exist on at least five physical folios
design.unit: cached exact A-B-A window with owner/target and structural-slot annotations

summary: Test whether exact A-B-A windows encode an interruption: the second A resumes the same active item or target after B, rather than being a generic repeated whole. The question is referent continuity, not a translation of A or B.
title: A-B-A frames resume the same active referent

design.binding: independent native panel-owner adjudication plus exact text occurrence joins on at least two held physical folios
design.contrast: same-panel label/prose pairs versus nearby-label and cross-panel matched controls with equal whole frequency
design.countermodel: Labels are reusable class or slot codes; pairings should follow proximity or section frequency and fail owner-held transfer.
design.mechanism: A label whole selects the specific prose item owned by its nearby panel; the same whole outside that panel need not select that item.
design.prediction: True pointer candidates recover the same owner or item field on held panels and at least two physical folios, while generic class-code controls do not.
design.related: GDT247 label-prose member reuse; GDT790 panel-owner overlay; GDT794 repeated labels; no token meaning changes implied
design.scope: admitted visual-owner spine and cached label/prose selectors; feasibility unknown where the panel has no singular native owner
design.unit: exact label/prose whole pair with native panel-owner relation

summary: Test whether a repeated complete whole used as a local diagram label points to the corresponding prose record member on the same panel or page, rather than functioning as a generic class code. The claim is an indexical pointer relation, not shared word translation.
title: Exact local labels point to a prose record member

design.binding: independent action/result annotations across at least five physical folios, with structural tags kept separate from lexical translations
design.contrast: candidate occurrences in action/result fields versus matched descriptive and label fields, stratified by section
design.countermodel: The whole is a generic content carrier whose apparent action association is caused by section or position; ordered framing should disappear under matched controls.
design.mechanism: The whole contributes an action modality that licenses an ordered operation/result frame, not merely a topic or item name.
design.prediction: A genuine operator has stable action-before-result framing and low descriptive-only usage on held folios; opaque carrier controls lack this ordered signature.
design.related: GDT744/GDT745 channel audits; GDT805 context-role discriminator; those routes do not select an operator modality as the target question
design.scope: cached structural tags and admitted prose/label selectors; feasibility unknown until action and result tags are independently bound
design.unit: complete whole in a cached field with independently tagged action, object, and result slots

summary: Test whether a candidate complete whole functions as an operation or instruction operator: its surrounding field should contain an action-bearing slot and a resulting state, while descriptive label fields should use a different frame. This distinguishes modality from a generic recurrent carrier.
title: A process operator whole selects action modality

design.binding: independent amount and material/operation annotations on at least five physical folios, with no component glosses used as labels
design.contrast: candidate whole on the material-side slot versus operation-side slot, matched within section and line position
design.countermodel: Adjacency is a layout convention or all nearby wholes are interchangeable; side-specific attachment should not transfer beyond discovery folios.
design.mechanism: An amount expression selects a material/part argument in one ordered slot; operation words occupy a distinct neighboring slot.
design.prediction: The measured-entity candidate recurs with independent amount frames and material/part tags on held folios, while the operation rival predicts process slots instead.
design.related: GDT760 amount-expression attachment; GDT804 bracket-middle audit; this proposal makes measured-entity versus operation the explicit rival
design.scope: cached exact amount expressions and admitted structural fields; feasibility unknown until amount direction and material tags are independently fixed
design.unit: amount expression plus adjacent complete-whole field and its ordered neighbors

summary: Test whether a complete whole adjacent to an amount expression denotes the measured material or part, rather than the operation that produces it. The prediction is a directional attachment relation with an explicit operation rival.
title: Amount expressions attach to a measured entity

design.binding: independent quality-state annotations on at least five physical folios and untouched held paths, retaining dry/moist rivals
design.contrast: dry-to-moist and moist-to-dry occurrences versus same-quality controls matched by section and position
design.countermodel: The transition pattern reflects section or page layout, with no semantic state operator; direction should vanish under matched same-quality controls.
design.mechanism: The whole is a state-change operator whose role depends on the ordered quality transition and predicts the next state-bearing field.
design.prediction: A state-change candidate predicts the direction and next state field across held folios; material-name and terminal rivals do not show directional transfer.
design.related: GDT625 ordered quality-state paths; GDT762 moist-medium discrimination; no cthy-specific claim is made
design.scope: cached quality-state paths and admitted exact-whole occurrences; feasibility unknown until quality tags are independently bound outside the discovery paths
design.unit: adjacent complete-whole pair or field crossing an independently tagged quality transition

summary: Test whether a candidate whole at a dry-to-moist or moist-to-dry transition denotes the resulting processed state, rather than naming the material or serving as a generic terminal. The contrast is directional state transition, not raw substring meaning.
title: A transition whole denotes processed state change

design.binding: independent record-boundary and topic/owner annotations across at least five physical folios, excluding line-end assumptions
design.contrast: records with a candidate initial whole versus matched records whose first field is a structural opener or opaque whole
design.countermodel: The initial whole is only a positional opener; later fields should show no topic continuity beyond section and record length.
design.mechanism: A record-initial whole introduces a topic that later compatible fields inherit without repeating an owner cue.
design.prediction: Candidate initial wholes predict later compatible item/part fields and fewer unexplained owner switches through the record, across held folios.
design.related: GDT581 structural parser limits; GDT791 record-boundary correction; distinct from drawing-reset and line-break hypotheses
design.scope: cached record-local fields and admitted owner-spine selectors; feasibility unknown where record boundaries remain inherited rather than independently bound
design.unit: admitted record with an initial complete whole, later fields, and independently tagged owner/topic changes

summary: Test whether a complete whole at a record's first field establishes the active item or material topic for later unmarked fields until an explicit topic change, rather than merely being a line-position marker. The target is record-level topic persistence.
title: Record-initial whole establishes a continuing topic

design.binding: independent action/result annotations and held folio split
design.contrast: candidate operation wholes versus matched material and terminal controls
design.countermodel: Apparent result proximity is record-length or section layout; latency excess disappears after matching.
design.mechanism: An operation licenses a short result latency in the local record.
design.prediction: At least 75% of held candidate occurrences have an independently tagged result/state within two fields, with a >=15-point excess over controls.
design.related: GDT702 immediate-right context; GDT625 state paths; this freezes a latency quantity
design.scope: cached complete fields; feasibility unknown until result tags are independently bound on five physical folios
design.unit: candidate occurrence and following two complete fields

summary: Quantify whether a candidate operation whole is followed by a result or state field within the next two complete fields, rather than being a generic carrier. The bound is prospective and keeps operation, material, and terminal rivals separate.
title: An operation whole predicts a near result field

design.binding: independent amount/material annotations across five physical folios
design.contrast: candidate measured-entity mapping versus matched operation frames
design.countermodel: Amount adjacency is ornamental or multi-valued; one-to-one conservation fails or matches operation controls.
design.mechanism: An amount expression binds one measured entity in its local field.
design.prediction: At least 80% of held amount frames have exactly one measured-entity attachment, with duplicate/zero rates below 10% each.
design.related: GDT760 amount attachment; GDT804 field bridge; quantitative conservation is the changed discriminator
design.scope: cached amount fields; feasibility unknown until amount direction and material tags are independently sourced
design.unit: independently tagged amount frame

summary: Test a quantitative necessary condition for a measured-material reading: each fixed amount frame should select exactly one material/part whole, while duplicate or zero selections should be rare. This distinguishes amount attachment from free local adjacency.
title: Amount frames conserve one measured entity

design.binding: independent human/diplomatic part captions on five physical folios, excluding proximity-only labels
design.contrast: part concentration for candidate whole versus frequency/section-matched opaque wholes
design.countermodel: The whole is a generic process or record carrier; part distribution is diffuse or section-driven.
design.mechanism: A material noun selects a stable part class in the working record system.
design.prediction: The candidate's top part accounts for >=70% of bound co-occurrences on at least four held folios and exceeds controls by 20 points.
design.related: GDT351 referent capacity; S104_HERBAL_COMPONENT_RELATIONS anchor; no species claim
design.scope: cached visual/text owner joins; feasibility unknown because singular part bindings are sparse
design.unit: candidate whole occurrence with an independently bound part label

summary: Test whether a candidate material whole has a stable association with one externally bound plant or body part across independent folios, rather than diffuse co-occurrence caused by section. The prediction is a concentration statistic with held folios.
title: A material whole recurs with one independently named part

design.binding: independent record-boundary and action annotations on five physical folios
design.contrast: candidate closure wholes versus terminal quality/material controls
design.countermodel: The whole is a result or material carrier; subsequent action rate is not reduced after matching field position.
design.mechanism: A closure whole commits the current record and prevents another unlinked action in the same record.
design.prediction: At least 80% of held candidate occurrences meet release-without-new-action, with a >=20-point excess over controls.
design.related: GDT556 closure route; GDT791 boundary correction; line ends are not used as boundaries
design.scope: cached record fields; feasibility unknown until boundaries are independently bound outside inherited parser assumptions
design.unit: candidate terminal occurrence through the next bound record boundary

summary: Quantify whether a candidate closure whole is followed by record release and no new action-bearing field before the next independently bound record boundary. This tests closure scope against a terminal-carrier rival.
title: A closure whole predicts record release without new input

design.binding: independent owner/reference annotations across five physical folios
design.contrast: first-owner mention versus later same-owner mention, matched by record position and section
design.countermodel: The whole has a fixed lexical or structural role; prior mention does not change owner-cue behavior.
design.mechanism: Reference status depends on discourse introduction versus prior mention.
design.prediction: At least 70% of later mentions preserve the prior owner without a new introduction cue, while first mentions show the cue at least 20 points more often.
design.related: GDT573 and GDT596 anaphoric routes; changed target is quantitative prior-mention conditioning
design.scope: cached record-local fields; feasibility unknown until owner/reference annotations are independently bound
design.unit: candidate whole occurrence with prior-owner history

summary: Test whether a candidate whole behaves like a definite first mention but an anaphoric reuse after the same owner/item has already been introduced, rather than having one fixed article-like function.
title: Prior mention switches a whole from definite to anaphoric use

design.binding: independent source-target relation edges on five physical folios, with alternate readers retained
design.contrast: source-before/target-after order versus reversed and no-argument controls
design.countermodel: Order is layout or section convention; reversed fields are equally common after matching.
design.mechanism: The action selects ordered source and target roles.
design.prediction: At least 75% of held action fields preserve the source-before-target order, exceeding reversed controls by 20 points across five folios.
design.related: GDT311 operation-event choice; GDT386 relation-edge capacity; this is a bounded semantic order claim
design.scope: cached action fields; feasibility unknown until source/target bindings are independent of the proposed order
design.unit: complete action field with independently bound source and target candidates

summary: Test whether a candidate action whole imposes a directional argument order: source/material precedes the action and target/result follows it, rather than neighboring arguments being freely permutable.
title: Action fields preserve source-to-target order

design.binding: independent modifier/head annotations across five physical folios
design.contrast: next-head compatibility versus prior-head and whole-field alternatives
design.countermodel: Modifier scope is global or backward; next-head preference disappears in interrupted sequences.
design.mechanism: The modifier has local forward scope over one head.
design.prediction: At least 70% of held modifier occurrences select the next head, with next-head excess >=20 points over prior-head controls.
design.related: GDT575/GDT577 modifier-scope history; this freezes a one-head quantitative rival
design.scope: cached modifier-bearing fields; feasibility unknown until head tags are independently assigned
design.unit: modifier-plus-head sequence with one or more neighboring heads

summary: Test whether a candidate modifier applies to the immediately following head, rather than the whole field or previous head. Repeated and interrupted modifier frames provide a quantitative scope discriminator.
title: A modifier whole scopes over the next head only

design.binding: independent native connector or diplomatic owner mapping on at least five physical folios
design.contrast: initial candidate versus matched non-deictic openers on panels with singular owners
design.countermodel: Initial forms are generic entry markers; owner resolution follows proximity or section frequency.
design.mechanism: The initial whole selects the external source currently being described.
design.prediction: At least 70% of candidate initial records resolve to the native source owner on held panels, exceeding opener controls by 25 points.
design.related: GDT699 deictic frame; GDT790 panel-owner overlay; no star-marker route is reopened
design.scope: admitted visual-owner spine and cached records; feasibility unknown because many apparent owners are proximity-only
design.unit: record-initial whole with native panel/source owner and subsequent record content

summary: Test whether a candidate record-initial whole is deictic to a visible panel, plant, or source location, rather than a generic opener. The prediction requires native owner evidence and held physical replication.
title: A record-initial whole points to the visible source

design.binding: independent amount/material annotations on five physical folios
design.contrast: different-material recurrence with stable unit slot versus material-name controls
design.countermodel: The whole names one material or process; cross-material recurrence is no higher than matched controls.
design.mechanism: The whole denotes a measure or unit that composes with multiple materials.
design.prediction: The candidate appears with at least three independently bound materials and retains the same unit slot in >=75% of held frames; material controls show concentrated one-material usage.
design.related: GDT593 unit/portion candidates; GDT760 amount attachment; distinct target is cross-material unit invariance
design.scope: cached amount expressions; feasibility unknown until material identities and unit slots are independently bound
design.unit: candidate whole across independently tagged amount frames

summary: Test whether a candidate unit whole can recur with different measured materials while preserving the same amount slot, distinguishing a unit/measure role from a material noun.
title: A unit whole recurs across amounts without naming material

design.contrast: candidate occurrence with a compatible antecedent versus matched occurrence lacking one, stratified by register
design.falsifier: No antecedent-rate difference on held records, or the effect is wholly explained by register/position, falsifies the bounded anaphoric mechanism.
design.mechanism: A reference whole points to an active prior item or result in the same record window; it is not freely inserted without an antecedent.
design.prediction: Reference candidates show a higher rate of compatible antecedents and continuation slots, with the effect surviving register and line position; a temporal/lexical model predicts no antecedent dependency.
design.related: OLOR identity peer review retains temporal versus anaphoric rivals; this proposal tests antecedent availability, not reading robustness or negative contexts
design.scope: cached admitted records and existing typed role annotations; feasibility_unknown for independent antecedent coding
design.unit: exact candidate occurrences with the preceding two fields and their typed source/result roles

summary: Test whether candidate reference-like wholes occur only when a compatible antecedent is available in the same bounded record, separating anaphoric use from a portable temporal or lexical reading.
title: Reference forms require an available local antecedent

design.contrast: same property with and without the candidate modifier, matched for owner/register and field position
design.falsifier: Paired contexts show no ordered degree contrast, or the apparent effect follows owner/register alone; no post-hoc threshold may be chosen.
design.mechanism: A degree operator composes with the immediately adjacent property field and leaves the property carrier unchanged.
design.prediction: The modifier changes the ordered degree class or threshold consistently within a source scope while preserving property identity; a material/action reading predicts no degree-specific shift.
design.related: Distinct from amount conservation and result latency: it asks compositional degree scope, not conserved quantity or timing
design.scope: existing admitted paired contexts only; feasibility_unknown for an independent ordinal degree scale
design.unit: complete modifier-property pairs with a fixed property candidate and an independently ordered comparison context

summary: Test whether a recurring modifier-like whole changes the interpreted degree of an adjacent property across paired records, rather than naming a material or acting as a generic connector.
title: Degree modifiers scope over an adjacent property

design.contrast: same whole in action-slot versus material/property-slot contexts, matched by owner and register
design.falsifier: No role-by-slot interaction on held occurrences, or it vanishes after whole identity and register controls.
design.mechanism: The compiler assigns role by argument position and neighboring field types while preserving the whole's local identity.
design.prediction: Successor and predecessor type constraints separate the two roles reproducibly, while a portable translation model predicts the same neighbor-type profile.
design.related: GDT633/GDT685 and GDT765 discuss role/context contrasts; this proposal tests a fixed whole's slot interaction without adding a decoder
design.scope: cached source cases with existing field-role annotations; feasibility_unknown for enough cross-slot repeats
design.unit: exact whole occurrences with two independently typed neighboring fields

summary: Test whether one complete recurring form is a process action carrier in one licensed slot but a material/property carrier in another, versus a single portable translation.
title: A fixed whole changes role with argument position, not meaning

design.contrast: same whole across two owners versus within-owner matched occurrences, controlling register and position
design.falsifier: Held-owner interaction disappears after position/register controls, or within-owner successors are not more coherent than cross-owner successors.
design.mechanism: The owner supplies a local referent namespace; the whole contributes a role and successor constraint within that owner.
design.prediction: Successor role distributions differ by owner for the same whole, while each owner retains an internally reproducible successor pattern; a portable-object model predicts no owner interaction.
design.related: GDT790/GDT791 owner overlays and GDT415 owner expansion are predecessors; this is a bounded interaction test, not a new owner atlas
design.scope: admitted visual-owner selectors and cached text only; feasibility_unknown for sufficient repeated wholes per owner
design.unit: admitted complete-whole occurrences with an exact visual owner and one following field

summary: Test whether a complete recurring whole keeps a stable semantic role while its referent is selected by the admitted visual owner, rather than denoting one portable object across the manuscript.
title: Owner-conditioned whole forms select local referents

design.contrast: within-panel continuation versus first occurrence after a panel boundary, matched by register and line position
design.falsifier: Held panels show no boundary interaction, or owner compatibility is unchanged after controlling register/position.
design.mechanism: A panel-local index binds to the active diagram unit and is reintroduced after a panel boundary.
design.prediction: After a boundary, candidate occurrences show renewed local-owner compatibility and reduced continuation to the prior panel; within-panel occurrences preserve the prior owner.
design.related: GDT790/GDT791 panel-owner work supplies boundaries but does not test deictic reset; distinct from line-break/reset and register-handoff proposals
design.scope: admitted visual selectors plus cached labels; feasibility_unknown for enough repeated candidate occurrences
design.unit: admitted panel boundary with adjacent label/prose occurrences of the candidate whole

summary: Test whether deictic-like complete wholes refer to the current visual panel and reset when a new panel begins, rather than carrying one global referent across adjacent panels.
title: Panel-local deictic forms reset at visual panel boundaries

design.contrast: part-specific association versus section- and page-matched candidate occurrences without that part
design.falsifier: No held-folio association survives section/page controls, or the top association changes with part-label coding, falsifies the bounded part-binding claim.
design.mechanism: The candidate denotes a plant-part class whose occurrences concentrate with externally bound root, leaf, seed, or flower records.
design.prediction: One candidate-part association replicates across held folios and alternate readings while unrelated part classes remain near baseline; a generic material or register marker predicts no specific part concentration.
design.related: IDEA000015 is a nearby raw predecessor; this proposal requires a preregistered external part index and held-folio association, not another co-occurrence count
design.scope: admitted botanical selectors and independent part index only; endpoint availability_unknown for sufficient cross-folio bindings
design.unit: complete candidate wholes paired with independently indexed botanical-part observations on separate folios

summary: Test whether a candidate whole is associated with an independently named plant part across held botanical records, distinguishing part identity from diffuse section co-occurrence.
title: A whole-word candidate binds one botanical part class

design.contrast: candidate-bearing versus candidate-free action contexts, matched by register and field position
design.falsifier: No held-context modal contrast after register/position controls, or an effect confined to one annotator's wording, falsifies the mechanism.
design.mechanism: A modal operator scopes over an adjacent action field and changes its obligation status without naming the action or material.
design.prediction: Candidate-bearing fields show higher rates of explicit requirement, prohibition, or conditional instruction in an independent medieval-style annotation, while descriptive contexts do not; a plain action reading predicts no modal shift.
design.related: GDT238 modal route and procedural automaton history are predecessors, but this is an independently scoped semantic modality question, not prefix decoding or grammar fitting
design.scope: cached admitted records plus preregistered independent modal annotation; endpoint availability_unknown
design.unit: complete action-like fields with independently coded procedural context and matched descriptive fields

summary: Test whether a recurring whole or construction marks required/forbidden action in procedural records, rather than merely describing an action or state.
title: Modal obligation is distinct from descriptive action

design.contrast: genre-stratified role distributions with leave-one-record-out validation, controlling register and position
design.falsifier: No held-record genre interaction, or the interaction disappears under record-level controls, falsifies the genre-conditioned role claim.
design.mechanism: The same whole may be a property/state marker in descriptive records but a procedure-condition marker in instructions because genre supplies a bounded role frame.
design.prediction: A candidate shows a reproducible role interaction with genre, while its neighboring field types remain within each genre; a single portable meaning predicts no interaction.
design.related: Existing q13 record-schema histories are broad comparators, not this candidate-level genre interaction; no decoder or regex-only test is proposed
design.scope: cached admitted record classifications and exact whole occurrences; endpoint availability_unknown for independent genre labels
design.unit: complete candidate occurrences in independently classified description and instruction records

summary: Test whether a candidate whole's semantic role differs between description records and instruction records, rather than assuming one portable translation across genres.
title: Record genre changes field-role distribution

design.contrast: candidate-bearing causal link versus matched sequential pair without the candidate, controlling record position
design.falsifier: No held conditional consequence contrast, or the effect is explained by record position alone, falsifies the causal-link mechanism.
design.mechanism: The candidate scopes over a preceding condition/action and licenses a dependent downstream state or field.
design.prediction: Following fields are more often state consequences conditional on the preceding event, with replication on held records; a simple sequence model predicts no dependency interaction.
design.related: Distinct from result latency, line adjacency, and transition-state proposals; retains sequential alternatives
design.scope: cached admitted event fields; endpoint availability_unknown for independent causal annotation
design.unit: complete candidate occurrences with a bounded preceding event and following state field

summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks a cause-to-consequence relation between adjacent record events, rather than merely listing two successive actions.
title: A causal connector predicts a dependent downstream state

design.contrast: explicit alternative pair with candidate versus matched paired fields without candidate
design.falsifier: No held alternative-structure contrast, or alternatives are not mutually exclusive under a blinded coding rule, falsifies the contrast mechanism.
design.mechanism: The candidate introduces or scopes an opposition whose two alternatives remain separately typed.
design.prediction: Candidate contexts show higher rates of mutually exclusive alternative structures and polarity reversal across the two fields; a generic connector predicts no alternative interaction.
design.related: Not negative-context exclusion, polarity retuning, or simple adjacency counting; alternatives must be predeclared
design.scope: cached paired fields only; endpoint availability_unknown for independent opposition coding
design.unit: candidate occurrences with two bounded alternative fields in the same record

summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks a contrastive branch between two alternatives, rather than serving as a generic connector or naming either alternative.
title: A contrast marker selects between explicitly opposed alternatives

design.contrast: candidate-bearing multi-item list versus matched adjacent item sequences without shared-predicate structure
design.falsifier: No held shared-predicate contrast, or list grouping depends on a single segmentation choice, falsifies the coordination mechanism.
design.mechanism: The candidate contributes coordination scope over a bounded list and leaves each item independently typed.
design.prediction: Candidate contexts show repeated shared-predicate/list structures and fewer independent predicate assignments; an item-noun model predicts no scope shift.
design.related: Distinct from amount frames, part cooccurrence, and role-position interaction; no quantity meaning is assumed
design.scope: cached bounded fields; endpoint availability_unknown for independent list-scope annotation
design.unit: candidate occurrences with two or more independently typed neighboring items and a shared predicate

summary: Test whether a recurring whole groups two or more neighboring items under one shared predicate, rather than being one item in the list.
title: A coordination marker scopes over a multi-item list

design.contrast: candidate-bearing reported fields versus candidate-free direct-observation fields, matched by register and field position
design.falsifier: No held provenance contrast after record controls, or the contrast follows one annotator's wording, falsifies the source-marker mechanism.
design.mechanism: The candidate scopes over a field's provenance and does not name the field's material or action.
design.prediction: Candidate-bearing contexts show a reproducible increase in source/report framing while local action and material roles remain unchanged; a lexical/content reading predicts no provenance interaction.
design.related: Different from modal obligation and genre interaction: provenance is source status, not command force or record type
design.scope: cached records plus external source-status coding; endpoint availability_unknown
design.unit: complete candidate occurrences in records with independently classified source/report status

summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks information provenance, distinguishing a reported/source-derived field from a directly observed or performed field.
title: A source marker separates reported from directly observed content

design.contrast: exception-marked divergence versus matched unmarked divergence and ordinary rule continuation
design.falsifier: No held override-and-return contrast, or divergence is equally common without the candidate, falsifies exception scope.
design.mechanism: The candidate scopes over a bounded exception and predicts a deliberate departure from the immediately established rule.
design.prediction: Candidate contexts show a higher rate of one bounded rule override followed by return or closure, while ordinary divergence lacks that pattern; a material/state reading predicts no override signature.
design.related: Different from line breaks, closure, and result latency; requires a predeclared rule pattern and no post-hoc exception labels
design.scope: cached repeated record patterns; endpoint availability_unknown for independent rule/exception coding
design.unit: candidate occurrences after a repeated rule pattern with a following divergent field

summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks an exception to an otherwise repeated local procedure, rather than naming a special material or state.
title: An exception marker licenses a local rule override

design.contrast: incoming/source-side occurrence versus outgoing/endpoint-side occurrence, matched by panel and register
design.falsifier: No held geometry interaction or no independent direction/terminal coding falsifies the distinction.
design.mechanism: The candidate's role is constrained by independently observed edge direction and terminal geometry.
design.prediction: Neighboring edge geometry separates instrument/channel from endpoint usage reproducibly on held panels; a single object meaning predicts no direction-by-terminal interaction.
design.related: Distinct from owner-conditioned referent and register handoff: tests geometric function, not ownership or presentation transition
design.scope: admitted visual selectors and direction metadata only; endpoint availability_unknown
design.unit: complete whole occurrences at admitted diagram edges with direction and terminal class independently coded

summary: Test whether a recurring whole refers to an instrument/channel when paired with an incoming edge but to an endpoint when paired with an outgoing destination, rather than one portable object meaning.
title: A diagram-linked whole distinguishes instrument from endpoint

design.contrast: state-linked recurrence versus biography/patient-linked recurrence, with owner and panel held out
design.falsifier: If independently owned labels preserve a person/patient identity while crossing apparatus or material states, or if state association disappears after owner masking, the process-state reference fails; this is distinct from visual enclosure capacity.
design.mechanism: A figure-associated whole is a process-state/material reference whose interpretation is selected by apparatus stage or material flow.
design.prediction: Held figure labels should track repeated material/process states or apparatus stages more consistently than person identity, patient identity, or literal bathing role.
design.related: Near GDT208 and closed BIO_FIGURE_INDIVIDUAL_ENCLOSURE_STATE; retains those limits and uses a different falsifier (state-versus-biography covariance, not enclosure counts).
design.scope: GDT208 primary comparison; independent endpoint availability_unknown because no singular Voynich label owner currently binds a readable value

source_evidence.quote: The q13 apparatus pages most plausibly describe a medicinal-alchemical circulation, separation, and staged-transformation system. Their human figures are provisionally better modeled as personified materials or process states inside an apparatus than as a literal catalogue of bathers.

design.unit: complete figure-associated labels with independently registered owner, apparatus stage, and material/process state

summary: Use the GDT208 external comparison as a source-grounded semantic discriminator: if q13 figures are personified materials or process states, a recurring figure-associated label should covary with apparatus/material state across independently owned panels, rather than with a stable human biography or patient identity.
title: Figure labels track process state rather than biography

design.contrast: repeated class/slot code versus unique-member/name or ordinal interpretations
design.falsifier: If a fixed complete form maps one-to-one to a named member or stable ordinal after owner masking, or if same-form occurrences have no shared slot/class property, the class-code hypothesis fails.
design.mechanism: A complete recurring form is a class/slot/system-entry code whose reference is to an organised position or class, not to one named object.
design.prediction: Across held panels, same-form reuse should coincide with shared slot/class properties and tolerate different members; masked-owner context should retain slot/class prediction but not recover one unique owner.
design.related: Near GDT793/GDT794 and existing IDEA026 panel-local reference; retained as a raw proposal with a different falsifier focused on cross-member class invariance, not rerunning the prior ordinal or owner screen.
design.scope: GDT793 primary report; endpoint availability_unknown because slot labels and semantic classes are not independently authored gold

source_evidence.quote: The result is 0/3. In other words, all apparent address evidence disappears when the candidate is forbidden from proving itself. The class/slot model does not predict such a companion fingerprint and survives this test.

design.unit: exact complete forms with independently recorded visual slot/class and owner-masked record context

summary: GDT793 reports exact okal collisions and a failed ordinal/owner reading. Test the narrower class-or-slot meaning by asking whether the same complete form recurs across multiple members sharing a slot/class while preserving local position, with no unique-owner recovery.
title: A repeated complete form codes a class or slot, not a unique member

design.contrast: argument-free successor with inherited carrier versus successor with a visible replacement argument; compare against a null model allowing silent carrier changes
design.falsifier: Any predeclared set of argument-free successors that systematically changes carrier value, or inherits an incompatible/empty value despite a fixed preceding carrier, falsifies the ellipsis rule.
design.mechanism: Argument values persist across an immediately following card only when no replacement argument is visibly written; OT/OL determines opening versus continuation, while the carrier value remains the same.
design.prediction: Argument-free successors preserve the preceding carrier value; visible Y/AIIN/AIN/OR successors replace it. The distinction should hold across the six observed OT/OL/DY envelopes.
design.related: Distinct from prior antecedent/reference and role-position proposals: this tests omission-based value inheritance inside an exact argument slot, not lexical anaphora, line breaks, genre, or portable translation. GDT559 is a primary predecessor whose 157/157 result motivates the question; the proposal retains that result as unconfirmed historical evidence.
design.scope: GDT559 observed state-card stream; independent semantic binding availability_unknown because the carrier labels remain working hypotheses, not externally authored meanings
design.unit: complete OT/OL state cards with a final visible argument and an immediate successor classified as argument-bearing or argument-free

summary: Use the observed OT/OL argument frames to test a bounded ellipsis rule: after a visible Y, AIIN, AIN or OR sets the current argument carrier, a following card without a new argument should reuse that value rather than silently selecting a new one.
title: An omitted argument reuses the current carrier value

design.availability: Independent stage/state and owner endpoint availability_unknown; the GDT214 source is an historical comparator only.
design.contrast: Cross-instance same-stage/state recurrence with changing local owner versus same-form recurrence tied to one object or owner.
design.falsifier: A preregistered held set in which repeated forms remain one-to-one with local owners, or where same-stage/state units do not share forms beyond the owner baseline, falsifies this component/state interpretation.
design.mechanism: A complete diagram-associated whole indexes a component or process state shared by parallel instances, rather than naming one physical object.
design.prediction: If the component/state-key hypothesis holds, a form should recur across multiple independently owned units sharing a stage/state and should tolerate owner substitution; a named-object model predicts stable owner identity or unit-specific forms.
design.related: Route-check returned GDT214, GDT718/719, GDT768, and GDT793. This remains distinct from IDEA000035 instrument-versus-endpoint geometry and IDEA000026/hu_class_slot_code class/slot membership: its falsifier is cross-instance state covariance under owner substitution, not edge direction, ordinal recovery, or class assignment.

source_evidence.quote:
Met 55.121.11 is the closest readable technical-rendering comparator yet.  It
combines a water source, repeated lifting components, a driving animal, shafts
and wheels, and numerous compact marks beside parts.  The reverse is
especially informative: four parallel lifting bays sit under a shared drive,
showing that repeated visual units can be components or stages of one machine
rather than four independent named objects.

design.unit: Exact complete wholes at independently admitted repeated visual units with separately coded stage/state and local owner.

summary: Use the GDT214 observation of repeated parallel machine bays to distinguish a diagram-local component/state reference from a named-object reading. The proposal asks whether the same complete whole recurs across distinct visual instances that share a machine stage or state, while its local owner changes.
title: A repeated diagram whole denotes a component or state key rather than an object

design.availability: Independent treatment-mode, figure-owner, and material-state endpoints availability_unknown; GDT210 provides only the comparator observation.
design.contrast: Candidate-bearing treatment-mode contexts versus matched candidate-free contexts, with figure owner and material state controlled.
design.falsifier: On a held, independently coded set, if the candidate tracks one figure/person or material across changing treatment modes, or shows no treatment-mode interaction after owner/material controls, the mode hypothesis fails.
design.mechanism: A recurring whole scopes a treatment-mode or procedure-position field; it does not denote the bather, person, or material undergoing treatment.
design.prediction: A mode marker should covary with one or more treatment actions/positions and remain portable across changing figures or materials; a person/material reading predicts stable figure or material association instead.
design.related: Route-check returned GDT210/GDT590-596 and GDT797. Distinct from IDEA000036 figure-label process-state covariance: this tests a procedural mode/position relation, not whether figures are personified materials versus biography; it also differs from IDEA000035 diagram edge direction.

source_evidence.quote:
1. q13 prose blocks should organize primarily by bath/pool installation or
   treatment episode, not one text label per drawn figure.
2. Figure pose and placement should covary with treatment mode—immersion,
   pouring, drinking, sweating, entry, or exit—more than with a fixed sequence
   of alchemical colors.
3. Independently recoverable flow direction should often be supply/drainage
   between bath levels, while only a minority of paths need form closed loops.

design.unit: Complete candidate occurrences in independently admitted visual/textual records with treatment-mode, figure-identity, and material-state annotations.

summary: Use the GDT210 comparator's explicit treatment-mode alternatives to test whether a recurring complete whole covaries with immersion, pouring, drinking, sweating, entry, or exit contexts while figure identity and material hypotheses are held separate.
title: A figure-linked whole selects treatment mode rather than a person or material

design.availability: Independent diagram graph, topology, owner, and component annotations availability_unknown; GDT209 is a comparator observation, not a Voynich label binding.
design.contrast: Candidate at return/junction topology versus candidate at terminal or ordinary component topology, with local owner and component class controlled.
design.falsifier: On a held graph-coded set, no return/junction enrichment after owner/component controls, or one-to-one association with a component or terminal endpoint, falsifies the topology-role hypothesis.
design.mechanism: A complete diagram-associated whole denotes a flow-topology role such as return, junction, or side outlet, and is selected by local graph position rather than by object identity.
design.prediction: A topology marker should recur at independently coded return or branching loci, including across changing local components; an object/instrument or endpoint model predicts stable component/owner or terminal association instead.
design.related: Route-check returned GDT209, GDT342/343, GDT523, GDT594, and IDEA000035/000039. This is related but distinct: it tests junction/return topology, not incoming-versus-outgoing endpoint role or repeated stage/state covariance.

source_evidence.quote:
Direct source-bound inspection found genuine quintessence-tradition machinery:

- Wolfenbüttel fol. 40r shows two connected pear-shaped vessels with crossing
  ducts;
- Othmer fol. 10r shows a return-loop vessel and a second vessel with paired
  internal descending ducts;
- Othmer fol. 36r shows paired domed furnaces, nested chambers, fire, and side
  outlets.

This is materially better evidence than a generic claim that medieval
alchemy used vessels. It supports circulation, paired-container, nested-
apparatus, and side-duct geometry as authentic technical imagery near the
Voynich period.

design.unit: Exact complete wholes at independently admitted diagram loci with source/return/junction/terminal topology coded before reading the whole.

summary: Use the directly inspected GDT209 return-loop, paired-duct, and side-outlet structures to test a topological relation reading for a recurring diagram whole: it marks circulation junctions or returns rather than naming an instrument, endpoint, or material.
title: A diagram whole marks a return-loop or branch junction

design.availability: Independent condition, applicability/license, and candidate-bound endpoint availability_unknown; GDT269 explicitly assigns no semantic operator or meaning.
design.contrast: candidate-bearing conditional applicability versus the same rule applied unconditionally or after a condition without the candidate; exception overrides and causal consequence are separate rivals.
design.countermodel: A renderer/template model can produce the same positive association if the candidate is simply an outer wrapper selected by PAGE_HOST or field position; GDT269's loss of strength under within-field-position conditioning is compatible with that model. Therefore a positional association alone cannot confirm conditional applicability.
design.falsifier: If the following rule occurs with equal authorization under failed and satisfied conditions, or the candidate only tracks record position/template while condition status adds no held interaction, the conditional-applicability hypothesis fails.
design.mechanism: A whole scopes over a precondition-to-applicability relation: the following rule is licensed only when the bounded condition holds.
design.prediction: The candidate should predict a stable interaction between the preceding condition and whether the following rule/action is licensed, with the rule absent or marked inapplicable when the condition fails; an unconditional wrapper/default predicts no condition-by-marker interaction.
design.related: Near IDEA000030 causal connector, IDEA000031 contrast marker, IDEA000032 coordination marker, and IDEA000034 exception override, but distinct in unit and falsifier: licensing an ordinary rule under a condition, not cause/consequence, opposition/list scope, or deliberate rule override.

source_evidence.quote:
This removes the simplest alternative that GDT267 merely compared different
host vocabularies on earlier and later records. The same opaque PAGE_HOST can
occur with q and bare rendering, and q remains earlier-associated within exact
page/host strata.

design.unit: Complete candidate occurrences with an independently coded preceding condition, following rule/action field, and a matched no-marker default context.

summary: Test whether a recurring whole marks that a following operation/field applies only when a bounded preceding condition is met, rather than being an unconditional action, generic connector, or exception override. GDT269's same PAGE_HOST with q and bare renderings supplies a source-informed conditioning question, not semantic gold.
title: A conditional applicability marker licenses a rule only under a stated context
